reader.requirement: An END PROGRAM header must be present for every program that contains another program and for every contained program; a single program, or the last of several separately compiled programs that contains nothing, may omit it. Because, without an intervening end program header, a following Identification Division header starts a CONTAINED source program (§1985:X.2.3.1 format, X.2.3.3 GR1b, X.2.5.4 GR4), a program without one followed by another program is a container and both need headers. 1985 also lets a container have no Procedure Division (X.2.3.1 prints separate brackets).

edition-consulted.switches: Year >= 2002 requires a Procedure Division before contained programs; at 85 the check is skipped (X.2.3.1 separate brackets)

reader.edition-search: EndMarkerPass.cs grepped for Edition.|Year|CobolVersion: only the EditionContext parameter used to position and emit COBOL2793; no edition comparison. The grammar rules programUnit/nestedProgram/endProgramHeader carry no edition predicate; the pass is called unconditionally from BinderDriver (line 90).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the 2023 rule also names a unit that merely PRECEDES another; under the 1985 structure such a unit is a container, so the same programs are refused; at 85 a container without a Procedure Division is accepted (2023 refuses it, COBOL2274)

reader.notes: The grammar makes nestedProgram's end header mandatory and ScreenProgram requires it of any programUnit with nested programs or a successor; every 1985 violation probed is refused and every legal omission accepted. For ep6/ep12 the message says 'precedes' (the 2023 reason) where the 1985 structure makes the unit a container; the refusal is right, only the stated reason is the 2023 one.
